steps.notes: Reference impl passes; targets = Pauli X/Y/Z (1j*R). Scaffold return line 'return Rz' contradicts docstring 'R' (minor D10).
Gate-recipe impl passes, BUT literal impl of the prompt's own formula expm(-1j*theta*kron(Sy,Sx))@|01> FAILS (global phase). Also zeros and 7.3x-scaled states PASS the fidelity check.
Reference impl passes, but all 3 targets are ~+1: constant return 1.0 and forgot-the-Z-operator <phi|phi> both PASS (D8).
Reference impl passes; targets -1.8302 (theta=0, matches hand calc g0+g1-g2-g3) and -1.28348. Tests 1 and 2 are byte-identical copy-pastes (same gl, same theta=pi/6, identical targets).

Reference impl (Nelder-Mead) and naive default minimize(x0=0) both pass. E(theta) is a single sinusoid whose minimum equals the exact GS energy to ~2e-8 for all 3 gl sets, so no optimizer/local-min trap.

findings.evidence: The step prompt defines the state as '|psi(theta)> = exp(-i theta Y_1 X_2)|01>'. The test asserts np.isclose(np.vdot(ansatz_o, ansatz_c), np.linalg.norm(ansatz_o)*np.linalg.norm(ansatz_c)) == True, which is GLOBAL-PHASE-SENSITIVE (requires ansatz_c to be a positive-real multiple of ansatz_o), and ansatz_o is built as expm(-1j*theta*kron(Sy,Sx)) @ (I (x) Rx(pi)) @ |00> = -i * exp(-i theta Y1X2)|01>. Verified dynamically: implementing the prompt's formula literally (state |01> = (0,1,0,0)^T) gives vdot = +1j instead of +1 -> steptest 59.2 FAIL (probe_literal.py); only the circuit construction that prepares |01> via Rx(pi) (picking up the unstated -i phase) passes (solution.py PASS). The background even asserts 'The Hartree-Fock state |01> can be obtained from |00> by acting the rotation Rx(pi) on the second qubit', which is itself only true up to the -i phase (Rx(pi)=-iX) -- the prompt text and the accepted target state differ by a physically meaningless global phase.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the test phase-insensitive: assert np.isclose(np.abs(np.vdot(ansatz_o, ansatz_c)), np.linalg.norm(ansatz_o)*np.linalg.norm(ansatz_c)) (and see the companion D8 fix for the norm). Alternatively state explicitly in the prompt that the HF state must be prepared by the gate Rx(pi) and that the resulting -i global phase is part of the expected output.

findings.evidence: The fidelity-style assert np.isclose(np.vdot(o,c), |o||c|) is vacuously true for c = zero vector (0 == 0) and is scale-invariant for positive multiples. Verified dynamically: create_ansatz returning np.zeros((4,1)) PASSES all 3 tests (probe_zeros.py), and returning 7.3*(correct state) PASSES (probe_scaled.py). The test never checks that the returned wavefunction is normalized or numerically equal to the target state.
findings.suggested_fix: Additionally assert np.allclose(np.linalg.norm(ansatz_c), 1) (or simply np.allclose(ansatz_c, ansatz_o) after fixing the phase issue with a phase-aligned comparison).

findings.evidence: All three h5 targets are ~ +1 (1, 0.9999999999999996, 0.9999999999999996): every test input was chosen so that the Z1 expectation is exactly +1, so the tests have no discriminating power. Verified dynamically: (a) the constant function 'return 1.0' PASSES all 3 tests (probe_const1.py); (b) the realistic bug measured_result = np.vdot(U@psi, U@psi) -- forgetting the Z operator entirely -- PASSES (probe_normbug.py). Such a wrong measureZ would then make a CORRECT step-59.4 implementation fail, mis-attributing the error to the wrong step.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace or add at least one test case whose Z1 expectation is not +1 (e.g. psi = |11> with U = I gives -1, or a superposition giving a fractional value such as 0.5).

findings.evidence: test_cases[1] and test_cases[2] are byte-identical (same gl = [-0.4804,-0.4347,0.3435,0.5716,0.0910,0.0910], same theta = np.pi/6) and their h5 targets are bit-identical (-1.2834833765112335). The step effectively has only 2 distinct test cases; theta=0 makes the g4 (Y1Y2) and g5 (X1X2) terms vanish, so those coefficients are constrained by a single probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the duplicated test 2 with a distinct input, e.g. a different theta (pi/3) or a different gl set.

findings.evidence: The provided scaffold return line is 'return Rz' while the docstring declares 'Output: R : matrix of shape(2, 2) The rotation matrix.' and the tests call rotation_matrices(1, pi) / rotation_matrices(2, pi) expecting Rx / Ry. A solver pattern-matching the scaffold's return variable could build only the Rz branch; the docstring and axis parameter disambiguate, so impact is low.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scaffold return line to 'return R'.

overall_assessment: The problem is solvable end-to-end: a solver that follows the background's gate recipe exactly passes all five steps, the final VQE landscape is a clean sinusoid whose minimum matches exact diagonalization, and there is no dependency drift or nondeterminism. The two real scoring risks are (1) step 59.2's phase-sensitive overlap test, which fails a mathematically correct implementation of the prompt's own closed-form definition exp(-i theta Y1X2)|01> because the frozen comparison state carries the -i global phase from the Rx(pi) Hartree-Fock preparation, and (2) step 59.3's tests, all of whose targets are ~+1, so trivially wrong implementations (constant 1, missing Z operator) pass and the resulting error is mis-charged to step 59.4. Both are fixable with one-line test changes.
